correctness.rationale: The model is sigma1=sigma4=0 in P5 over characteristic two, not the alternate normalized five-coordinate model. Solving sigma1 for x5 and computing the Jacobian gives the vanishing pattern via the common derivative cubic; geometric singularities split into 15 projective two-ones points and 30 projective (a,a,b,b,c,c) points with a,b,c the three elements of F4*, so the F2/F4 Frobenius action is 15 fixed points plus 15 pairs. I independently enumerated the projective F2 and F4 points, obtaining 15 and 205, and the singular subsets of cardinalities 15 and 45. Independently expanding the quadratic tangent form at each orbit representative gives invertible rank-four polar forms, hence ordinary double points; the nonsplit rational-node exceptional quadric has 5 F2 points, while both types have 25 F4 points. Each node blowup contributes #Q(Fq)-1 versus one original point: at odd extension degrees 15 q^2, at even degrees 45 q^2+90q, with q=2^d. Translating these counts by log zeta gives [(1-4T)^30(1+4T)^15(1-2T)^45(1+2T)^45]^{-1}. The all-degree arithmetic uses the proved geometric orbit/split classification, not an extrapolation from F4 enumeration. Does not compute the full zeta of the singular threefold or all arithmetic twists.

originality.rationale: The 2016 geometric paper already identifies the sigma1=sigma4 symmetric model and its geometric 45 nodes, so those are not claimed new. Bruin–Nasserden (2018) computes the zeta of a different normalized five-coordinate model B and explicitly says symmetric B' is a nontrivial twist when primitive cube roots are absent (Section 2, p. 5). Since F2 has no primitive cubic root, its zeta and node Frobenius data cannot simply be transferred to B'. The inspected 2018 text does not compute B'(F2), the splitness of its exceptional quadrics or this blowup quotient. Bruin–Filatov (2022) explicitly excludes characteristic two. Best-of-knowledge O passes for the characteristic-two twist's explicit arithmetic correction, not geometric existence of 45 nodes.
residual_risks: Historical descriptions of arithmetic reductions of the symmetric Burkhardt model could identify the same split/non-split exceptional data under another nomenclature.
The original geometric 45-node count is firmly prior, and the four-factor result is only a quotient for the singular-point blowup, not a full zeta formula of B'.
The characteristic-two model cannot be identified with Bruin–Nasserden B using an algebraic-closure isomorphism alone.

value.rationale: The special fiber at residue characteristic two distinguishes arithmetic models of a classical singular Fano threefold; the fact all 15 F2 points are nodes and resolution yields 75 rational points is a natural and surprising local-global boundary. The all-extension Frobenius/eigenvalue correction for the exceptional divisors is an exact natural arithmetic invariant, not an arbitrary finite sample. Complete zeta of the singular model and the classification of all twists remain outside the theorem.

final_claim: Over F2 the symmetric sigma1=sigma4 complete intersection in P5 has precisely 45 geometric ordinary nodes: 15 F2-rational nodes and 15 Frobenius pairs, all 15 F2 points singular and nonsplit. Its blowup in all singular points has 75 F2 points and an explicit four-factor zeta quotient.
